Vector-Jacobian product

Source: R/ad.R
vjp.Rd

Port of jax.vjp.

Usage

vjp(fun, ..., has_aux = FALSE, saveable_args = TRUE, in_nzs = NULL)

Arguments

fun

Function of pytrees of arrays.

...

Primal arguments.

has_aux

Whether fun returns list(output, aux).

saveable_args

A tree of logicals, a prefix of the list of primal arguments like in_nzs, by default TRUE: which arguments may be kept for the backward pass. An argument array that the backward pass needs as it is (not a value computed from it) and that is marked FALSE is not kept: vjp_fun$args_res shows a NotSaveable() sentinel in its place, and the value must be put back (vjp_fun$args_res[[i]] <- x) before vjp_fun is called. Arguments the backward pass does not need show NotNeeded(). Only jaxR arrays given as arguments count; R numbers are converted to new arrays, like Python scalars in JAX.

in_nzs

Optional tree of logicals, a prefix of the list of primal arguments (for example list(TRUE, FALSE)): which inputs may have a nonzero tangent. The tangent of an input marked FALSE is a symbolic zero during linearization, and its cotangent is zero. The default marks every input.

Value

list(out, vjp_fun) (plus aux when has_aux), where vjp_fun(ct) returns a list of cotangents, one per primal argument. ct must have the structure of out, and each of its leaves the shape and dtype of the matching output (as in JAX there is no broadcasting or casting; the cotangent of an integer output is ignored). vjp_fun$out_nzs is a tree of logicals with the structure of out (plain lists in place of registered containers) telling which outputs have a tangent that is not known to be zero, and vjp_fun$args_res holds the saved arguments (see saveable_args).
